title: Artificial intelligence–derived splenic response in cardiac positron emission tomography is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events: a multi-site study
summary: higher ratio independently associated with MACE and mortality after covariate adjustment, including patients with preserved myocardial flow reserve.
ai_technology: fully automated AI derived splenic uptake stress/rest ratio from PET in six-site REFINE registry.
organization: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine Research Center, Departments of Biomedical Sciences, Medicine, and Cardiology, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, 6500 Wilshire Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90048, USA; Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Southern California, Los Angeles, CA, USA; Department of Cardiac Sciences, University of Calgary, Calgary, Alberta, Canada

evidence.tested: higher ratio independently associated with MACE and mortality after covariate adjustment, including patients with preserved myocardial flow reserve. Retrospective linked-outcome cohort across six sites with 3.4-year median follow-up; association does not establish causation.
evidence.ai_role: fully automated AI derived splenic uptake stress/rest ratio from PET in six-site REFINE registry.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
